nodes.v: Most records pass through a dozen hands. These pathways exist because one person can carry an idea from the first line to the final master — and know, at every stage, what the next one needs.
Writing, playing and finishing records for artists, labels and publishers — at any point from a blank page to a delivered master.
Sessions as a writer in the room, or a co-write built around an artist already holding the idea. Multi-platinum credits behind it, no house style imposed on top of it.
Taking a song from demo to finished record — arrangement, players, sound and the decisions in between. Equally available as additional production on something already underway.
Engineering with a writer's ear: capture decisions made for the song, not the session sheet. Attended or remote, with files delivered ready for the next stage.
Mixes that serve the record rather than a genre template — including the instrumental, clean and TV versions that sync and screen work will ask for later.
Final masters prepared to platform specification, with the consistency a release or catalogue needs across every destination.
Guitar on charting records and on stage in front of festival crowds. Booked as a player, remotely or in the room.
Original music written to image, and existing work placed into it. Credits across Paramount, CBS, ABC, Disney, Warner Bros., HBO and Showtime.
Score written to picture, from a single cue to a full series. Themes that survive the edit changing underneath them.
A catalogue built for supervisors, plus bespoke reworks when a cue nearly fits. Rights and splits documented before a cue is sent, not after.
The finishing a broadcaster or platform will actually accept — stems, versions, loudness and paperwork, delivered to the spec sheet the first time.
Sound as part of an identity rather than a layer added at the end — for brands, fashion houses, and cultural and experiential work.
A mark in sound: a short signature plus the system of variations that keeps it recognisable across a film, a store, a handset and a stadium.
Music written for a campaign and its whole family of edits, cleared on terms agreed up front.
Runway, film and installation sound built to the room and the running order — composed, not compiled from a playlist.
Partnerships with designers, artists, photographers and directors where the music is authored alongside the work rather than licensed into it.
Scripted and spoken formats treated with record-making craft — the difference between a show that sounds produced and one that sounds recorded.
An original theme and the family of stings, beds and transitions that make a series feel like one thing week to week.
Underscore for narrative and documentary work, placed to carry the story rather than fill the gaps.
Dialogue cleaned, levelled and mastered to platform loudness, so the show holds up in a car, on earbuds and on a kitchen speaker.
Decades of studio experience, made available directly.
A second ear on a record, a catalogue, a roster or a room — short engagements where judgement is the deliverable.
Not sure which of these it is? Describe the project.
Most work spans several of these. Say what you are making and the shape of it will be clear enough.
